title: Horse Registry
subtitle: Pedigree, ownership, documents and medical status of every horse
summary: The Horse Registry records each horse with its pedigree, its ownership structure over time (shares must total exactly 100 %), its documents with checksums and its medical records. It answers the two questions racing depends on: may this horse run on this date, and who owned it that day?

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A horse joins the register as PENDING. It can only become ACTIVE when the ownership in force today totals exactly 100 %; activation charges the registration fee to the largest owner through an accounting event (reference HREG-<registration no>).

Ownership is effective-dated. Changing the structure ends the current rows the day before the new ones start, so the registry can answer 'who owned Midnight Rose on race day?' long after the fact. Prizes depends on exactly that answer.
Medical records can withdraw a horse until a date and time. While withdrawn, the eligibility API says no, and Race Operations refuses the entry.

sections.title: Horse Registry database architecture · Visual ERD
sections.intro: The physical MySQL 8 model contains four Horse Registry tables, seven declared foreign keys and a shared relationship to enterprise_core.party. The two pedigree references point back to the horse table itself.

sections.title: Seven foreign keys explained in plain English
sections.intro: A foreign key is simply a database-enforced reference: the child row points at an existing parent. Nullable links are optional; ON DELETE RESTRICT protects referenced records.
rows: A horse can identify its father in the same registry (optional).
A horse can identify its mother in the same registry (optional).
Each ownership share belongs to a registered horse.
Each owner is a shared person or organization, not a duplicated contact.
All documents remain attached to their registered horse.
Veterinary observations and withdrawal records belong to a horse.
An optional veterinarian relationship uses the shared party register.

sections.title: Business story · one horse, several owners, one race day
paragraphs: Why this model matters: A race result is not the end of the business process. The club may need to determine whether the horse was allowed to race, who owned it on that date, who should receive prize money, and why those answers are auditable months later.

Step 1 — register the horse. horse supplies the permanent registration number, name, sex, breed, status and optional sire/dam references. The same horse row acts as the stable anchor for related data.

Step 2 — record ownership with validity dates. horse_ownership associates the horse with an Enterprise Core party, a percentage and effective dates. Rather than overwriting last year's owner, new rows allow the service to answer historical ownership questions.

Step 3 — manage documents and veterinary status. horse_document stores document location, checksum and verification or expiry metadata. horse_medical_record keeps recorded veterinary history and a possible withdrawal_until timestamp.

Step 4 — authorize the racing workflow. Race Operations can ask Horse Registry for eligibility, and Prizes can consult ownership as at the race date. Registration fees may trigger an accounting event passed through the integration outbox and eventually posted by the GL.

sections.title: What MySQL enforces versus what the business service enforces
sections.intro: A critical enterprise architecture distinction: a foreign-key or CHECK constraint is not the same thing as a multi-row business invariant.
rows: Two horses cannot share the same registration number.
Every individual ownership row must have a valid share.
Yes · effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to >= effective_from
An ownership period cannot end before it starts.
Referential integrity is enforced across schemas on this MySQL server.
All current ownership shares total exactly 100%
The Academy demo describes a service/database guard; this aggregate rule requires implementation beyond the listed CHECK constraints.

sections.title: Video walkthrough · from the screen to the database
items: Start with the question: “Who owned this horse on race day, and why can the system prove it?” Show the full-size ERD before opening the live Horse Registry application.
Locate the source of truth: Show horse as the anchor, then point to its two pedigree self-references (sire_id, dam_id).

Explain historical ownership: Follow horse_ownership to the shared party master. Discuss owner shares, effective_from, effective_to and the difference between a row-level CHECK and a 100% aggregate rule.
Demonstrate trust and safety: Show document checksum metadata, a veterinary withdrawal, and the resulting eligibility decision in the live UI/API.
Follow the enterprise consequence: Explain how horse activation and registration fees connect to AR/GL, while race-day ownership is consumed later by Prizes & Settlement.
Close with an architecture lesson: Regulatory or financial questions are answered by effective-dated records and immutable/auditable history, not by the latest value in a screen.

sections.title: Design decisions
items: Effective dating instead of overwriting: history is the feature, not an afterthought.
Eligibility is a live REST call from Race Operations, because a medical withdrawal can happen minutes before an entry.
The 100 % rule exists twice: in the service for a friendly message, and as a database trigger so no path can break it.
